rounds.q: Cat fans call these ‘toe beans’. What are they?
rounds.why: Toe pads cushion each step, and cats sweat through their paw pads. Damp paw prints on the vet’s table are a thing.

rounds.q: Kangaroos often use their ___ like a fifth leg.
rounds.why: When grazing, a kangaroo leans on its tail as an extra leg. It pushes with real force.

rounds.q: Bees mostly smell with these. What are they?
rounds.why: A bee’s antennae are covered in smell and touch sensors. They’re basically its nose.

rounds.q: Dolphins breathe through…
rounds.answer: A blowhole on top of the head
rounds.why: Dolphins are mammals, so they surface to breathe air through a blowhole.

rounds.q: Name the highlighted part.
rounds.why: Long, webbed back feet make frogs strong swimmers and champion jumpers.

rounds.q: This bumpy pink patch is as unique as a fingerprint. What is it?
rounds.why: Each cat’s nose leather has its own pattern of ridges and bumps, a bit like a fingerprint.

rounds.q: A turtle’s shell is…
rounds.answer: Bone, fused to its ribs and spine
wrong: A separate case it can leave
rounds.why: The shell is part of the skeleton. A turtle can no more leave its shell than you can leave your ribcage.

rounds.q: An elephant’s trunk is a nose joined with its…
rounds.why: It’s nose and upper lip in one, with no bones and a huge number of muscle bundles.

rounds.q: Which animal has three hearts and blue blood?
rounds.why: Two hearts pump blood through the gills, one pumps it round the body. Crabs have blue blood but just one heart. The first permanent artificial heart was fitted on this day in 1982.

rounds.q: Name the yellow lump on the back leg.
rounds.why: Bees pack pollen into a hair-fringed hollow on each back leg to carry it home.

rounds.q: A giraffe’s hoof is about the size of a…
rounds.why: Giraffe hooves can be about 30 cm across. A kick from one can be dangerous to a lion.

rounds.q: A flamingo’s ‘backwards knee’ is actually its…
rounds.why: The real knee is hidden up under the feathers. The joint you see bend is the ankle.

rounds.q: How many compartments does a cow’s stomach have?
rounds.why: Rumen, reticulum, omasum and abomasum. Grass takes a long journey.

rounds.q: The hard outer rim is made of the same stuff as your nails. What is it?
rounds.why: Hoof wall is keratin, like fingernails, so trimming it doesn’t hurt.

rounds.q: Name the highlighted claw higher up the leg.
rounds.why: The dewclaw is the cat’s first digit, the equivalent of your thumb. Handy for gripping prey.

rounds.q: The highlighted openings are the owl’s ears. Why is one higher?
rounds.answer: To pinpoint sounds up and down
rounds.why: In owls like the barn owl, lopsided ears let them locate a mouse in total darkness.

rounds.q: Why can’t crocodiles stick their tongues out?
rounds.answer: A membrane holds it to the floor of the mouth
rounds.why: The tongue is tied down. A flap at the back of the throat seals out water instead.

rounds.q: Sea stars have no blood. What moves around inside instead?
rounds.why: A water-filled plumbing system powers the tube feet and moves things around.

rounds.q: A cheetah’s claws…
rounds.why: Always half out, they work like running spikes for grip at top speed.

rounds.q: Name the highlighted part.
rounds.why: The sole is slightly cupped, so it doesn’t take the full weight. The wall does that.

rounds.q: Name the highlighted organ.
rounds.why: The ink sac squirts a dark cloud through the siphon, a smokescreen for a quick escape.

rounds.q: Roughly what share of an octopus’s neurons are in its arms?
rounds.why: Each arm can taste, feel and react with surprising independence. Group project energy.

rounds.q: A narwhal’s tusk is…
rounds.why: It’s a long spiral tooth, usually the left one, growing through the upper lip.

rounds.q: How many sets of molars does an elephant go through in a lifetime?
rounds.why: New molars move forward from the back like a slow conveyor belt. When the last set wears out, eating gets hard.

rounds.q: Name the balloon that puffs up under the chin.
rounds.why: Male frogs inflate a vocal sac to make their calls louder. Some can be heard a kilometre away.

rounds.q: When an octopus swims, its main heart (the middle one)…
rounds.why: The body heart pauses while it jet-swims, which may be why octopuses prefer crawling.

rounds.q: Mantis shrimp eyes have about how many types of colour receptor?
rounds.why: We have three. They have about 12, but oddly don’t seem better at telling colours apart.

rounds.q: The backward-facing spines on a cat’s tongue are hollow. Why?
rounds.answer: To wick saliva deep into fur
rounds.why: Scoop-shaped tips soak up saliva and deliver it to the skin during grooming.

rounds.q: What is this small highlighted slit at the base of the ear for?
rounds.why: Henry’s pocket may help with hearing high-pitched sounds or let the ear fold. Science shrugs.

rounds.q: A honeybee’s wings beat about how many times a second?
rounds.why: Around 230 beats a second, which is where the buzz comes from.

rounds.q: Elephants flap these mainly to…
rounds.why: Elephant ears are full of blood vessels. Flapping them cools the blood, like a giant fan.

rounds.q: Which animal can regrow lost legs, and even parts of its heart?
rounds.why: Axolotls regrow limbs, tail, spinal cord and more, with barely a scar. Our mascot is very proud.

rounds.q: How many bones are in a giraffe’s neck?
rounds.why: Seven, the same as you. Theirs are just enormously long.

rounds.q: Name the highlighted part.
rounds.why: Only female bees have a stinger. It’s a modified egg-laying tube.

rounds.q: Name the highlighted slits.
rounds.why: Water flows in through the mouth and out through the gill slits, which pull oxygen out on the way.

rounds.q: How many wings does a honeybee have?
rounds.why: Two on each side. In flight, each pair hooks together to work as one.

rounds.q: Snakes ‘smell’ by flicking their…
rounds.why: The forked tongue collects scent particles and delivers them to a sensing organ in the roof of the mouth.

rounds.q: Why are flamingos pink?
rounds.why: Chicks hatch grey. Pink pigments from algae and shrimp gradually colour the feathers.

rounds.q: Frogs use these to help them swallow. What are they?
rounds.why: When a frog swallows, its eyes sink down into its head and help push food down its throat. Yes, really.

rounds.q: Name the highlighted part.
rounds.why: Talons are curved claws for gripping prey. Owls can even swing one outer toe backwards for a better grip.

rounds.q: These knobbly things on top: what are they called?
rounds.why: Ossicones are bony knobs covered in skin and fur. Both males and females have them.

rounds.q: Deer antlers are made of…
rounds.why: Antlers are bone, shed and regrown every year. Horns, like a cow’s, are permanent.

rounds.q: Name the highlighted dish-shaped face.
rounds.why: The facial disc works like a satellite dish, funnelling sound towards the ears.

rounds.q: Which bird can fly backwards?
rounds.why: Hummingbirds twist their wings in a figure eight, so they can hover and even reverse.

rounds.q: Lose one, grow a new one. What is it?
rounds.why: Sea stars can regrow lost arms. It takes months, but it’s still a better repair plan than ours.

rounds.q: This line along the side helps the shark sense…
rounds.why: The lateral line feels tiny ripples and vibrations, like a struggling fish nearby.

rounds.q: A dolphin’s blowhole is really its…
rounds.why: The nostril migrated to the top of the head over millions of years. Very convenient for breathing at the surface.

rounds.q: Name the highlighted part.
rounds.why: A honeybee’s long tongue (proboscis) works like a straw for slurping nectar.

rounds.q: Chameleons can move their eyes…
rounds.why: Each eye can look somewhere different, then both lock on when it’s time to strike.

rounds.q: Name the highlighted part.
rounds.why: Whiskers are deep-rooted touch sensors packed with nerves. Never trim them.

rounds.q: The highlighted ring is the octopus’s brain. What’s odd about it?
rounds.answer: It wraps around the food pipe
rounds.why: The doughnut-shaped brain surrounds the oesophagus. Swallow something sharp and it goes through the middle of the brain.

rounds.q: Bar-headed geese fly on migration over which mountains?
rounds.why: Their blood grabs oxygen extra tightly, so they cope with air that would leave us gasping. Today is International Mountain Day.

rounds.q: This has a tuft on the end, perfect for swatting flies. What is it?
rounds.why: Giraffe tails are around a metre long, and that hairy tuft makes a handy fly swat.

rounds.q: Over a lifetime, a shark can get through about how many teeth?
rounds.why: Rows of spare teeth move forward to replace lost ones, conveyor-belt style.

rounds.q: Sea cucumbers breathe through their…
rounds.why: They pump water in and out of the rear end to feed branching ‘respiratory trees’ inside.

rounds.q: Why do cats’ eyes glow in torchlight?
rounds.answer: A mirror-like layer behind the retina
rounds.why: The tapetum lucidum bounces light back through the eye for a second go. Great for night vision.

rounds.q: A woodpecker’s long tongue, when tucked away…
rounds.why: The tongue bones loop round the back of the skull and may help cushion all that hammering.

rounds.q: The giraffe’s front ‘knee’ (highlighted) is really its…
rounds.why: Same in horses. The front ‘knee’ is the wrist. The real knee is higher up, near the body.

rounds.q: Why does a worker honeybee usually die after stinging you?
rounds.why: The barbs lodge in skin, and the stinger rips away from the bee. Queens have smooth stingers.

rounds.q: A snail’s teeth are found…
rounds.why: The radula is a rasping ribbon with thousands of microscopic teeth.

rounds.q: In basking sharks, the liver can be about what share of body weight?
rounds.why: Up to around 20 to 25%. Oil is lighter than water, so it works like a built-in float.

rounds.q: A horse’s hoof is really one giant…
rounds.why: Horses walk on the tip of one middle toe. The hoof is a supersized toenail.

rounds.q: What’s special about the hair on a sloth?
rounds.why: Grooves in the hairs hold algae, which may give a greenish camouflage. Sloth fur also grows from belly to back, so rain runs off when they hang upside down.

rounds.q: About how many whiskers does a cat have on its muzzle in total?
rounds.why: Usually 12 a side, in four rows. The top two rows can move independently of the bottom two.

rounds.q: How do many sea stars eat a mussel?
rounds.answer: Push their stomach out into the shell
rounds.why: They prise the shell open a crack, slide their stomach in and digest dinner on the spot.

rounds.q: What are elephant tusks, really?
rounds.why: Tusks are giant front teeth (incisors) that keep growing. Elephants use them for digging, lifting and showing off.

rounds.q: What colour is a polar bear’s skin?
rounds.why: Under the pale fur, polar bear skin is black.

rounds.q: Name the highlighted V-shaped part of a horse’s hoof. Yes, really.
rounds.why: It really is called the frog. It’s a rubbery pad that grips and absorbs shock.

rounds.q: Butterflies taste with their…
rounds.why: Taste sensors on their feet tell them if a leaf is right for laying eggs.

rounds.q: Name the long, dark purple part.
rounds.why: A giraffe’s tongue is about 45 to 50 cm long and tough enough to wrap around thorny acacia branches.

rounds.q: Name the highlighted part of the octopus.
rounds.why: Octopuses have eight arms, not tentacles. Squid and cuttlefish have eight arms plus two longer tentacles for snatching prey.

rounds.q: Which animal has the biggest heart?
rounds.why: A blue whale’s heart has been weighed at about 180 kg.

rounds.q: How many legs does an insect have?
rounds.why: Six legs, three body parts. Spiders, with eight legs, aren’t insects.

rounds.q: Name the highlighted pointy bits.
rounds.why: Cats keep their claws tucked away until needed, which keeps them sharp and makes walking silent.

rounds.q: Frogs don’t drink with their mouths. How does most water get in?
rounds.why: Many frogs soak up water through a thin ‘drinking patch’ on the belly and thighs.

rounds.q: These three tiny dots on top of the head are…
rounds.why: Bees have five eyes: two big compound eyes and three simple eyes on top.

rounds.q: Horses can’t do which of these?
rounds.why: A tight valve where the food pipe meets the stomach means horses almost never vomit. Bad news for colic.

rounds.q: Name the highlighted whiskers.
rounds.why: Touch these and the cat blinks: an early warning system for twigs and nosy fingers.

rounds.q: What colour is octopus blood?
rounds.why: It uses a copper-based protein called haemocyanin to carry oxygen, which turns it blue.

rounds.q: Name the two rounded parts at the back.
rounds.why: The heel bulbs are soft and springy, helping cushion every landing.

rounds.q: These pointy tufts on top of the head are…
rounds.why: ‘Ear tufts’ are just feathers, probably for camouflage and showing mood. The real ears are hidden at the sides of the face.

rounds.q: Many bird bones are hollow inside. What fills them?
rounds.why: Air sacs from the lungs reach into some bones, making them light and part of the breathing system. Humans first flew a plane on this day in 1903.

rounds.q: Where is a sea star’s mouth?
wrong: At the tip of an arm
rounds.why: The mouth is on the underside, right in the centre. The highlighted spot is directly above it.

rounds.q: Dolphins sleep by…
rounds.answer: Resting half their brain at a time
rounds.why: One half of the brain sleeps while the other keeps watch and remembers to breathe.

rounds.q: This can swivel to point almost backwards. What is it?
rounds.why: Cats have around 32 muscles in each ear, so they can aim them like radar dishes.

rounds.q: Name the highlighted tube.
rounds.why: Water squirts out of the siphon for breathing and jet propulsion. It’s also how the ink gets aimed.

rounds.q: Hippos ooze a reddish liquid. It’s…
rounds.why: Nicknamed ‘blood sweat’, it’s neither. It helps block sun and may fight germs.

rounds.q: A male platypus has a venomous spur on its…
rounds.why: Painful for people, though not deadly. Rare among mammals.

rounds.q: How do many frogs help push food down?
rounds.answer: They pull their eyes down into the mouth
rounds.why: The eyeballs press down on the roof of the mouth, nudging food towards the throat.

rounds.q: An owl’s eyes aren’t balls. What shape are they?
rounds.why: Long tube-shaped eyes gather lots of light, but can’t move. So the head does the moving.

rounds.q: Why are owls almost silent in flight?
rounds.why: Comb-like edges and velvety feathers break up the turbulence that makes wing noise.

rounds.q: A platypus has no…
rounds.why: Its food pipe connects straight to the intestine. No acid stomach needed.

rounds.q: In male bullfrogs, this highlighted eardrum is…
rounds.why: A male bullfrog’s eardrum is larger than its eye; a female’s is about eye-sized.

rounds.q: Shark skin is covered in tiny…
rounds.why: They’re called dermal denticles: skin teeth. They cut drag and feel like sandpaper backwards.

rounds.q: Each of these neck bones can be about how long?
rounds.why: Each giraffe neck vertebra can top 25 cm. Seven of those adds up.

rounds.q: Name the highlighted sieve-like plate.
rounds.why: It lets seawater into the sea star’s plumbing that powers its tube feet.

rounds.q: Which mammal can have up to 10 neck vertebrae?
rounds.why: Most mammals have seven. Three-toed sloths have extra, manatees and two-toed sloths fewer.

rounds.q: A shark’s tail has a bigger upper lobe. What does that do?
rounds.answer: Gives lift as well as push
rounds.why: The lopsided tail pushes the shark forwards and slightly up, which helps without a swim bladder.

rounds.q: Why is a giraffe’s tongue so dark?
rounds.why: The leading theory: dark pigment stops sunburn during hours of browsing in the sun.

rounds.q: Why can cats squeeze through tight gaps?
rounds.why: A cat’s tiny collarbones aren’t attached to other bones, so the shoulders can narrow. If the head fits, the cat usually fits.

rounds.q: Compared with yours, a giraffe’s blood pressure is about…
rounds.why: Pumping blood two metres up to the brain takes serious pressure. Thick-walled arteries and tight leg skin stop swelling.

rounds.q: Which part of a jellyfish does the stinging?
rounds.why: Tentacles are lined with tiny harpoon cells that fire on contact, even after the jellyfish has died.

rounds.q: What is a rhino’s horn made of?
rounds.why: Rhino horn is packed keratin, the same stuff as hair and nails. No bone at all.

rounds.q: The fin that terrifies swimmers. Name it.
rounds.why: The dorsal fin on the back keeps the shark steady so it doesn’t roll over.

rounds.q: Owls can’t roll these in their sockets. What are they?
rounds.why: An owl’s eyes are fixed in place, so it swivels its whole head instead. Very dramatic.

rounds.q: Hidden where the arms meet is a hard…
rounds.why: A parrot-like beak is the only hard part of an octopus, so it can squeeze through any gap its beak fits through.

rounds.q: Which Australian animal leaves cube-shaped droppings?
rounds.why: Wombat intestines squeeze droppings into neat cubes. Handy for marking territory on rocks without them rolling off.

rounds.q: Which animal has sideways, rectangular pupils?
rounds.why: Wide, horizontal pupils give grazing animals a panoramic view for spotting predators.

rounds.q: Name the highlighted bits at the front of the foot.
rounds.why: Elephants walk on tiptoe. A thick fatty cushion inside the foot takes the weight.

rounds.q: Name the highlighted fin.
rounds.why: Pectoral fins work like aeroplane wings, giving lift and steering.

rounds.q: These tiny things run under each arm. What are they?
rounds.why: Hundreds of water-filled tube feet let a sea star creep along and grip rocks.

rounds.q: Jellyfish have no…
rounds.why: Just a loose net of nerves. No brain, no heart, no bones. Still extremely effective.

rounds.q: Name the puffy highlighted part.
rounds.why: Most cats have 24 muzzle whiskers, 12 a side in four rows, rooted in these pads.

rounds.q: Sharks use these only for smelling, not breathing. What are they?
rounds.why: Shark nostrils are dead-end pockets for smelling. Breathing happens through the mouth and gills.

rounds.q: What’s unusual about a koala’s front paws?
rounds.why: Koalas have two digits that work like thumbs on each front paw. Ideal for gripping branches.

rounds.q: Name the highlighted fin.
rounds.why: The tail fin sweeps side to side to push the shark forwards.

rounds.q: Do penguins have knees?
wrong: No, their legs are straight bones
rounds.why: Penguin knees sit up inside the body under the feathers. Hence the waddle.

rounds.q: The round patch behind the eye is the frog’s…
rounds.why: Frogs wear their eardrums on the outside. It’s called the tympanum.

rounds.q: Where are a garden snail’s eyes?
rounds.answer: On the tips of its long tentacles
rounds.why: The eyes sit on top of the longer pair of tentacles. Tap one and it rolls back in.

rounds.q: Owls can turn their head about how far?
rounds.why: About three-quarters of a full turn either way. Not quite a full horror-film spin.

rounds.q: How many neck vertebrae does an owl have?
rounds.why: Owls have 14 neck bones, twice our seven. Hence the swivel.

rounds.q: What’s unusual about a kiwi’s nostrils?
rounds.answer: They’re at the tip of the beak
rounds.why: Kiwis sniff out worms underground with nostrils right at the end of their long beak.

rounds.q: Which Australian turtle can breathe through its bottom?
rounds.why: This Queensland turtle absorbs oxygen through its rear end (the cloaca), so it can stay underwater for ages.

rounds.q: Giraffe ossicones are…
rounds.answer: Bone covered in skin and fur
rounds.why: They start as cartilage and turn to bone, then fuse to the skull. Never shed.

rounds.q: What are these little cups along the arm?
rounds.why: Each sucker grips on its own, and it’s packed with chemical sensors, so an octopus tastes whatever it touches.

rounds.q: Name the thin pale band between the wall and the sole.
rounds.why: Farriers use the white line as a guide: nails go in outside it.

rounds.q: Name the yellow lump on the back leg.
rounds.why: Bees pack pollen into a hair-fringed hollow on each back leg to carry it home.

rounds.q: A chameleon’s tongue can reach up to about…
wrong: A tenth of its body length
rounds.why: It fires out in a fraction of a second, with a sticky tip that grips prey.

rounds.q: An ostrich’s eye is bigger than its…
rounds.why: Around 5 cm across: the biggest eye of any land animal.

rounds.q: About how long is a giraffe’s tongue?
rounds.why: Long enough to wrap round thorny branches, and to clean its own nostrils. Charming.

rounds.q: The highlighted organ helps keep a shark from sinking. What is it?
rounds.why: Sharks have no swim bladder. A huge oily liver adds lift. In basking sharks it can be a quarter of body weight.

rounds.q: A hummingbird’s heart can beat more than ___ times a minute.
rounds.why: Over 1,200 beats a minute in flight. At night it can slow right down to save energy.

rounds.q: Elephants have a hidden ‘sixth toe’ in each foot. What is it?
rounds.answer: A rod of cartilage and bone
rounds.why: This ‘predigit’ props up the foot’s fatty heel pad, a bit like a hidden high heel.

rounds.q: How many neck vertebrae does a manatee have?
rounds.why: Manatees are rare mammals with fewer than seven. They can’t turn their heads much.

rounds.q: Worker bees make wax from glands on their…
rounds.why: Four pairs of wax glands on the underside of the abdomen produce thin wax flakes.

rounds.q: Bees mostly smell with these. What are they?
rounds.why: A bee’s antennae are covered in smell and touch sensors. They’re basically its nose.

rounds.q: Which of these mammals lays eggs?
rounds.why: Platypuses and echidnas are monotremes: mammals that lay eggs.

rounds.q: Cat fans call these ‘toe beans’. What are they?
rounds.why: Toe pads cushion each step, and cats sweat through their paw pads. Damp paw prints on the vet’s table are a thing.

rounds.q: Name the highlighted part.
rounds.why: Long, webbed back feet make frogs strong swimmers and champion jumpers.

rounds.q: A camel’s hump is mostly…
rounds.why: The hump stores fat for energy. Camels cope with thirst in other clever ways.

rounds.q: An elephant’s trunk is a nose joined with its…
rounds.why: It’s nose and upper lip in one, with no bones and a huge number of muscle bundles.

rounds.q: Kangaroos often use their ___ like a fifth leg.
rounds.why: When grazing, a kangaroo leans on its tail as an extra leg. It pushes with real force.

rounds.q: Dolphins breathe through…
rounds.answer: A blowhole on top of the head
rounds.why: Dolphins are mammals, so they surface to breathe air through a blowhole.

rounds.q: The hard outer rim is made of the same stuff as your nails. What is it?
rounds.why: Hoof wall is keratin, like fingernails, so trimming it doesn’t hurt.

rounds.q: This bumpy pink patch is as unique as a fingerprint. What is it?
rounds.why: Each cat’s nose leather has its own pattern of ridges and bumps, a bit like a fingerprint.

rounds.q: What do the two smaller highlighted hearts do?
rounds.why: They’re branchial hearts. The bigger one in the middle then sends that oxygen-rich blood around the body.

rounds.q: Name the highlighted pores on the shark’s snout.
rounds.why: Named after Stefano Lorenzini, who described them in 1678. They sense electric fields.

rounds.q: A few stiff hairs grow near this highlighted pad. What are they called?
rounds.why: Mystacial are the muzzle ones, superciliary over the eyes and genal on the cheeks. Carpal whiskers sense wriggling prey.

rounds.q: Which tongue papillae give a cat’s tongue its hollow, scoop-tipped spines?
rounds.why: Filiform papillae are the rough, backward-hooked ones. Their hollow tips wick saliva into the fur.

rounds.q: What is a honeybee’s pollen basket properly called?
rounds.why: A scopa is the pollen brush of many solitary bees, a tegula covers the wing base and a pulvillus is a foot pad.

rounds.q: Elephants flap these mainly to…
rounds.why: Elephant ears are full of blood vessels. Flapping them cools the blood, like a giant fan.

rounds.q: Do snakes have eyelids?
rounds.answer: No. A clear scale covers each eye
rounds.why: That clear scale (the brille) is shed with the skin. It’s why snakes seem to stare.

rounds.q: Where are a cricket’s ears?
rounds.why: Crickets hear through eardrums on their front legs. Imagine listening with your shins.

rounds.q: This big, baggy part looks like a head. What is it really?
rounds.why: The mantle is a muscular bag holding the hearts, gills and gut. The actual head, with eyes and brain, sits just below it.

rounds.q: A giraffe’s hoof is about the size of a…
rounds.why: Giraffe hooves can be about 30 cm across. A kick from one can be dangerous to a lion.
